newsitem.title: NORWAY: Sleipner West output flows despite repairs-Statoil.
newsitem.headline: Sleipner West output flows despite repairs-Statoil.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday it was undertaking repairs and modifications at the separation plant on the Sleipner West gas condensate platform but production was being maintained.

Gas began flowing at the Sleipner West development at the end of August, one month ahead of schedule. The gas forms part of the deliveries under the Troll agreements to continental Europe via the Zeepipe line to Zeebrugge in Belgium.

The development comprises two platforms, the unmanned Sleipner B wellhead unit and the T gas treatment installation. The T-platform will reduce the level of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the gas as required under sales specifications.

About one million tonnes per year of CO2 will be removed and disposed of by injecting it about 1,000 metres below the seabed. The project is the largest development to inject CO2 and is also is the first time it has been injected at an offshore platform.

Statoil said the repairs were to the plant which separates carbon dioxide from gas production. The separation columns failed to operate at full capacity during the commissioning phase of the North Sea installation.
Fine-grained sand had also blocked the well used to inject the CO2, the Status Weekly newsletter said.
The well and one of the two separation columns should be back on line in about one week, Statoil said.

"Production from Sleipner West is being maintained, with the unseparated gas reinjected into the Sleipner East reservoir. The repair work will have no effect on exports to continental Europe because Sleipner East output is uninterrupted," Statoil said.
Recoverable reserves at Sleipner West are estimated at 127 billion cubic metres of gas and 325 million barrels of condensate and NGLs.
